This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 02-11-2023 at about 8:00 p.m., the petitioner was standing beside the road to cross, observing traffic rules and norms, opposite Nature Autoni Company on Sarjapura-Attibele Road, Bidraguppe Village, Bengaluru.

At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing number TN-70-AH-8955 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was riding at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
3. As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru, where he received first aid treatment.

Based on medical advice,
he was subsequently shifted to Oxford Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
4. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead a normal life as he did prior to the accident.
The petitioner claims to have incurred expenses of Rs. 2,00,000 towards medical treatment, medicines, conveyance, and incidental charges.
5. At the time of the accident, the petitioner was 19 years old, working as a mason and earning Rs.18,000 per month.
He submits that due to the injuries, he has suffered a loss of earning capacity and income.
It is the petitioner's specific contention that the accident occurred solely on account of the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle.

6. Accordingly, the petitioner prays that suitable compensation be awarded against Respondent No.
1 and 2, being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle.

7. Respondent No.1 appeared through counsel and filed a written statement admitting the issuance of a two-wheeler package policy, but contended that their liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
They denied the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and further submitted that the rider did not possess a valid driving license at the time of the accident.
8. Respondent No. 1 also denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and highlighted a delay in lodging the complaint.
They disputed the nature of the injuries, the petitioner's occupation, income, and the claimed amount of compensation, terming the claim as excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 1 prayed for the dismissal of the petition.

9. Respondent No. 2 denied all the allegations made by the petitioner.
They contended that the alleged accident did not occur due to rash and negligent riding by the offending vehicle.

Instead,
they argued that the accident happened due to the negligence of the petitioner, who allegedly tried to cross the road while watching a mobile phone and without observing traffic rules.

10. Respondent No. 2 further stated that, as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No. 1, the policy was valid, and the rider of the offending vehicle was in possession of a valid driving license.
Based on these grounds, Respondent No. 2 prayed for the dismissal of the petition against them.
11. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-70-AH-8955 by its rider, in RTA took place on 02-11-2023 at about 8.00 p.m. on Sarjapur Attibele Road,
Opp. Nature Autoni, Company Bidaraguppe Village, Attibele Hobli, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award ?
12. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case

,
doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

13. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 14. ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on on 02-11-2023 at about 8:00 p.m., the petitioner was standing beside the road to cross, observing traffic rules and norms, opposite Nature Autoni Company on Sarjapura-Attibele Road, Bidraguppe Village, Bengaluru.
At that time, the rider of the offending motorcycle was riding at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell and sustained grievous injuries.

15. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner himself was examined as PW-1 and produced the following documents: FIR at Ex. P-1, FIS at Ex. P-2, Police Intimation at Ex. P-3, Spot Mahazar at Ex.P-4, IMV Report at Ex. P-5, Wound Certificate at Ex. P-6, and Charge Sheet at Ex.P-7.

Further, Dr. D.S. Ramachandra was examined as PW-2, who produced two documents marked as Ex P-13 and P-14.
17.

As per the medical records at Ex. P-6, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
 Laceration over the anterior aspect of the right leg,  Swelling and deformity of the right leg,  Hemothorax,  Fracture shaft of the right humerus,  Fracture of the right tibia and fibula, and  Fracture of the 7th, 8th, 10th, 11th, and 12th ribs.
The doctor opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
18. The version of PW-1 is consistent with the averments made in the petition and is corroborated by contemporaneous police records.
The Investigating Officer, after due investigation, filed a charge sheet fixing responsibility on the rider of the offending motorcycle.
19. During the course of cross-examination, it was suggested to PW-1 that he had fallen elsewhere and that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident, which he categorically denied.
Except for this suggestion, nothing material was elicited in his cross- examination to discredit his testimony.

Significantly, Respondent No. 2 has not produced any credible evidence to substantiate their plea that the petitioner sustained injuries elsewhere or that the offending motorcycle was not involved in the accident.

No independent witnesses have been examined on their behalf, nor were any contrary investigation records produced or proceedings initiated to challenge the charge sheet before the competent authority or court.
20. Thus, the defence remains a mere bald suggestion unsupported by material evidence.

It is a well-settled principle that in Motor Accident Claim Proceedings, the petitioner is not required to prove negligence beyond a reasonable doubt as in criminal cases; the standard of proof is that of preponderance of probabilities.

Applying this principle, the oral testimony of PW-1, coupled with the contemporaneous police documents such as the FIR, FIS, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, and charge sheet, conclusively establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner has successfully proved Issue No. 1, and the same is answered in the affirmative.

1. Laceration over the anterior aspect of the right leg,
2. Swelling over the right leg,
3. Deformity on the right side,
4. Hemothorax,
5. Fracture shaft of the right humerus,

7. Fracture of the 7th, 8th, 10th, 11th, and 12th ribs.
22. The doctor opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained multiple grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Sri Sai Hospital,
wherein he received first aid treatment, and based on the advice of the doctor, he was shifted to Oxford Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient.
23. PW-2, Dr. S. Ramachandra, Orthopaedic Surgeon and DNB-PG Teacher at General Hospital,
Jayanagar, Bengaluru, deposed that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident and was treated as an inpatient at Oxford Hospital, Bengaluru.

He stated that the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
 Closed mid-shaft fracture of the right humerus,  Open fracture mid-shaft of the right tibia and segmental fracture of the right fibula (Type III-A),  Multiple rib fractures with haemopneumothorax on the right side, and  Anterior iliac bone fracture on the right side.
24. He further stated that the petitioner underwent CRIF with IMIL nailing for fracture of the right tibia and ORIF with plates and screws for fracture of the right humerus.
PW-2 clinically and radiologically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the permanent physical disability.
25. On examination, the petitioner complained of difficulty in standing on both legs, walking on plain surfaces and slopes, climbing stairs, kneeling, and sitting cross-legged or squatting.

PW-2 assessed the total disability of the right lower limb at 33.52% and the whole body disability at 16.76%.
26.

It is pertinent to note that the injuries sustained by the petitioner to the right tibia and right humerus have resulted in restricted mobility, and since both the tibia and humerus are weight-bearing and functionally crucial bones, any impairment at these sites hampers not only day-to-day activities but also affects the petitioner's ability to perform occupational tasks.
27.
However, PW-2 has not expressed any opinion regarding the functional disability, i.e., the actual impact of the injuries on the petitioner's earning capacity.

Taking into account the medical evidence,
the site and nature of injuries, the petitioner's age, and probable occupational requirements, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the functional disability may be fairly assessed at 10% to the whole body for the limited purpose of determining the compensation towards future loss of earning capacity.
28. On perusal of the petition and the documents produced, it is observed that the petitioner has mentioned his age as 19 years.

Though no independent document was submitted to substantiate the same, the copy of the Aadhaar card and medical records on file corroborate that the petitioner's age Shankar Kumar vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157930733/
5 is indeed 20 years.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appropriate multiplier for the purpose of computing compensation is 18, in accordance with the principles laid down in Sarala Verma case.
29. The petitioner has stated that he was employed as a Mason,earning a sum of Rs. 18,000 per month.
He claims that, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has suffered a loss of earning capacity and future income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence to substantiate his income from this employment.
30. In the absence of concrete evidence relating to the petitioner's income, the Tribunal is required to adopt the notional income as per the guidelines of Lokadalat.
Considering that the accident occurred in the year 2023, the petitioner's notional monthly income is assessed at Rs.16,000/- for the purpose of calculating compensation.

31. Accordingly, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner, having sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
32. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 10% is reasonable and just.
33. The petitioner was 20 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 18 x 10/100= Rs.3,45,600/- towards loss of future income.
34. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head of Pain and sufferings 35. Loss of amenities of life:
undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under the head of loss of amenities of life.
36. Medical expenses:

Under the head of pecuniary damages relating to treatment, hospitalization,
and medicines, the petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex P-10 amounting to Rs. 1,07783/-.
The Tribunal finds the medical bills to be genuine and admissible.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to Rs.1,07,783/- towards medical expenses.
37. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has stated that the petitioner requires two more surgeries for removal of implants.
However, no estimate has been produced to substantiate the cost of the proposed surgery.
In the absence of material evidence regarding the cost of the future surgery, this considers it is just and reasonable to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses.

Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges: On perusal of Ex.P.9 & 10 - Discharge summary, which show that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Sri Sai hospital, Bengaluru,
from 02-11-2023 to 03-11-2023 and at Oxford hospital, Bengaluru, from 03-11-2023 to 22-12-2023 i.e, totally for a period of 51 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .50,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
39. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery,
this tribunal considers the 4 months for rest is considered .
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 4 = Rs.64,000/-. loss of earning during laid up period.
